newsitem.title: SPAIN: POLL-Bank of Spain rate cut seen Friday after CPI.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Bank of Spain rate cut seen Friday after CPI.

text.p: Spanish April CPI, coming in Wednesday at a lower-than-expected 1.7 percent year-on-year, gave analysts a clear signal the Bank of Spain will cut its 5.5 percent money market rate by 25 basis points as soon as Friday.

Ten financial experts polled by Reuters after the inflation data was released predicted the central bank will reduce its official rate for the fourth time this year at its next repurchase auction on Friday.
One said the rate cut could be as much as 50 basis points.
The other nine analysts said the bank has scope for a more aggressive reduction of 50 basis points but it was likely they would leave some room for further moves before the summer.
They expect Spanish CPI to reach its nadir in May followed by another 25-basis-point reduction.

Good inflation performance was the main argument in favour of further easing but a new wave of Euro-optimism after the European Union commission gave its approval to Spain's convergence plan was also supporting market expectations.
Analysts said the increased probability of Spain being in Europe's first group forming the single currency would also bring down the short-term rate spread over Germany.
The German repo rate is at 3.0 percent compared to 5.50 percent in Spain.
The Bank of Spain started the current easing cycle on December 1995 when it cut the rate by 25 basis points from 9.25 percent.
